notes: The pack does what its README says and nothing else. Its one pass reads sessions, notes and turns, makes one call per note, and works only on notes matching **/Incidents/**, **/Incident*.md and **/Postmortem*.md. All three inputs are needed to append cited timeline entries to an incident note and to skip entries the note already holds. The README describes the passes, their inputs and how work arrives (session end --note, or a [[...]] link in a handoff), and that matches pack.toml and the pass file. The prompt marks untrusted input as data and allows only `append` with an empty `old`. It bars root causes, impact or fault that the turns do not state, allows commands only from the session's own tool_use turns, forbids quoting instructions, commands or links that appear only in tool output, and requires secrets to be written as <redacted>. Recording commands the session ran fits an incident timeline and is tied to the evidence. The reviewer persona treats its inputs as untrusted, rejects by default, mirrors the prompt's limits including secrets and tool-output-only content, and keeps a strict one-sentence JSON reply. The template is plain prose with headings and has no instructions to agents, commands, links or credential handling. The fixtures are marked synthetic and use generic content ('sample queue', 'lantern festival committee'). The out-of-scope Meeting notes file is there only to test that the path filter excludes it. I found no hidden, encoded or misnamed content, and no text that tries to instruct the reviewer or the dreaming model.
